correctness.rationale: The inverse of the original multiplicative generator is a logarithm of a rational function. Its exponential-series coefficients are w_k=q^k(1+(-1)^(k+1)alpha^k)/(k theta). When alpha<=1 all are nonnegative and sum exactly to 1; the resulting conditional-independent mixture constructs a copula in every finite dimension. For alpha>1, w_2<0, and exponential tilting plus uniqueness of finite signed Laplace transforms precludes complete monotonicity, hence all-dimensional canonical validity by McNeil--Neslehova. A rational third-derivative test at alpha=100, exp(theta)=3 proves trivariate failure. Executed checker.py confirms finite algebraic/numerical identities; proof is analytic rather than based on experiments.

value.rationale: The 2023 family is introduced as a bivariate dependence model, for which higher-dimensional Archimedean validity is a structural feasibility question. The sharp alpha<=1 threshold and explicit positive integer mixing distribution permit multivariate construction and simulation for any dimension, identify an odd-only frailty boundary, and show a bona fide bivariate member failing already in dimension 3. They supply a usable modeling classification rather than routine renaming or a narrow arbitrary slice.
